questions.answer: A wave that transfers energy from place to place.
accepted_alternatives: A travelling wave that transfers energy.

marking_points.text: States that a progressive wave transfers energy from place to place.

option_feedback.A: This confuses the travelling pulse with the local rope material.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The mark moves locally as the pulse passes and returns near equilibrium.
option_feedback.C: The mark must move while the rope section is disturbed.
option_feedback.D: The mark does not drift steadily along the rope.

marking_points.text: Selects B, identifying local motion followed by return near equilibrium.

option_feedback.A: Correct. A progressive ripple transfers energy while there is no net transport of water across the tank.
option_feedback.B: Water particles move locally, but water is not carried from source to leaf overall.
option_feedback.C: The ripple transfers energy, not a net amount of water to the leaf.
option_feedback.D: The moving leaf is evidence that energy reached it.

marking_points.text: Selects A, identifying energy as the transferred quantity.

option_feedback.A: The coils do not travel with the compressed region to the far end.
option_feedback.B: The disturbance travels; it is not fixed.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The pattern travels while each coil has local motion.
option_feedback.D: Both the disturbance and individual coils move, but in different ways.

marking_points.text: Selects C, distinguishing the travelling disturbance from local coil motion.

parts.answer: The light ring moves when the pulse arrives.
accepted_alternatives: The pulse causes the ring at the far end to move.

marking_points.text: Identifies movement of the distant ring as evidence that energy reached it.

parts.answer: Neighbouring rope sections interact and pass the disturbance onward. Each section moves locally about equilibrium, so the disturbance and its energy travel even though the rope material has no net motion to the ring.
accepted_alternatives: A description of successive neighbouring sections setting one another into motion, with no net transport of rope.

marking_points.text: Explains that neighbouring rope sections pass the disturbance onward through their interactions.
States that each rope section moves locally or returns near equilibrium while energy travels.

parts.answer: The ripples travel from the paddle towards the absorber. The cork moves locally about its equilibrium position and remains near the same region of the tank.
accepted_alternatives: Ripple fronts move across the tank while the cork oscillates or bobs locally.

marking_points.text: States that the ripples or disturbance travel across the tank towards the absorber.
States that the cork moves locally about equilibrium and is not carried across the tank.

parts.answer: The moving absorber shows that the ripples have transferred energy to it. Therefore the ripples are progressive waves that carry energy from the paddle to a new place.
accepted_alternatives: Energy reaches the absorber and causes it to vibrate.

marking_points.text: Uses the absorber's vibration as evidence that energy reached it.
Concludes that the progressive ripples transfer energy from place to place.

parts.answer: The pulse travels along the rope from left to right. Bead Q moves locally as the pulse passes and then returns near its equilibrium position rather than travelling with the pulse.
accepted_alternatives: Q oscillates locally while the pulse propagates along the rope.

marking_points.text: States that the pulse travels along the rope from left to right.
States that Q moves locally and returns near equilibrium rather than travelling with the pulse.

parts.answer: Bead P and nearby rope sections interact with successive neighbouring sections, passing the disturbance onward. Energy therefore travels with the progressive pulse until R is made to move, while P remains near its original place.
accepted_alternatives: Successive local motions pass the disturbance and energy to R without net transport of P.

marking_points.text: Explains that successive neighbouring rope sections pass the disturbance onward.
Explains that energy reaches R while P has only local motion and no net travel to R.

parts.answer: A labelled bead returns near its original horizontal position after the pulse has passed.
accepted_alternatives: The pulse reaches R while P remains near its original place.
Each bead moves only while the pulse passes it.

marking_points.text: States an observation showing a labelled rope element remains local while the pulse travels onward.
